From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

Team / Harper —

I pulled the attached one-pager into a short worked example based on Harper's CSV. High-level technical assumptions (conservative / target):

- avg prompt tokens (user -> model input): 320 tokens
- avg response tokens (model output): 100 tokens
- baseline tokens per round-trip: 420 tokens (320+100)
- typical convo length in pilot: 3 turns => 3 * 420 = 1,260 tokens per user-session (rounds)

Caching (prefix / KV) assumptions:
- conservative hit: 15% (many unique follow-ups)
- target hit: 35% (reused prompts & templated completions)
- effective tokens with caching = baseline_tokens * (1 - hit_rate) + cached_overhead ~ 420 * (1 - hit_rate) + 20
  - example target: 420 * 0.65 + 20 = 293 tokens per call average

Batching/concurrency impact:
- no batching: baseline latency SLO met but higher compute per token (reference unit-cost factor = 1.0)
- modest batching (2–4 requests/batch): typical 1.25x efficiency (per-token compute cost reduced by ~20%)
- aggressive batching (8+): up to 1.8x efficiency but adds 40–120ms queueing latency depending on traffic shape

Price mapping (illustrative):
- baseline GPU-backed model compute cost mapping => $0.0006 per token at small scale (reference internal rate)
- with target caching (35%) and modest batching (2.0x effective efficiency), effective cost per token = 0.0006 * (1 - batching_saving) * (1 - caching_factor) — simplified worked example below.

Worked example (target case):
- baseline tokens per session: 1,260 tokens
- effective tokens per session after caching: 1,260 * 0.65 = 819 tokens
- batching efficiency 1.25x (i.e., costs reduced by 20%): effective tokens-equivalent = 819 / 1.25 = 655 tokens-equivalent
- cost per session = 655 * $0.0006 = $0.393 => ~ $0.39 per active session

Sensitivity notes:
- if cache hit drops to 15%: tokens/session -> 1,071 -> /1.0 (no batching) -> cost ~ $0.64/session
- Warm-up week: 1.25x multiplier on token burn (KV coldness + prefetch testing) — plan for a 25% higher spend in week 1

Operational asks for MAP (these are action items we recommend adding):
- Datum to provide a 1-week rolling sample of anonymized prompts (we got the CSV — still need daily qps by endpoint)
- Redwood to run a 48-hour preflight sim against pilot traffic shape (we'll estimate cache-hit distribution)
- Set an SLO for mean latency: 150ms P50 / 400ms P95 (with modest batching) — confirm if Datum's product can tolerate up to +80ms for better token economics

Attachment: redwood-unit-econ-works.pdf (worked example, charts)

Let me know if you want the calc sheet exported as CSV. I can add more latency vs. unit-cost curves.

—Mateo
Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
